BUS.G12.T1.CREATIVE.A1.title: Creative thinking in complex contexts
BUS.G12.T1.CREATIVE.A1.description: Applying creative thinking and advanced problem-solving skills to respond to challenges in dynamic and complex business contexts and case studies, building on the problem-solving cycle and techniques from earlier grades.
BUS.G12.T1.CREATIVE.A1.strand: T1 — Legislation, Human Resources, ethics, creative thinking & business strategies
BUS.G12.T1.CREATIVE.A1.recovery_strategy: Complex problems need creative thinking: generate several options, weigh them against the real business situation, and choose the best. Advanced problem-solving combines techniques rather than relying on one fixed answer.

questions.question: A complex business problem usually has:
options: Several possible solutions to weigh up
Only the answer in a textbook
questions.expected: Several possible solutions to weigh up
questions.memo: Complex problems rarely have a single right answer; they call for generating and weighing several possible solutions.

questions.question: Creative thinking helps a business respond to _________ and changing situations.
questions.memo: Creative thinking is especially valuable when situations are complex and constantly changing.

questions.question: True or false: Advanced problem-solving may combine several creative-thinking techniques.
questions.memo: Tough problems often need more than one technique, combined, to generate and test good solutions.

questions.question: Which of these is a creative-thinking technique?
questions.memo: Brainstorming generates many ideas freely, making it a creative-thinking technique.

questions.question: A real business situation presented for analysis and solving is called a case _________.
questions.memo: A case study presents a real or realistic business situation to analyse and solve, testing applied thinking.

questions.question: True or false: In complex business contexts there is rarely a single 'correct' answer.
questions.memo: Complex contexts usually allow several reasonable responses, so judgement is needed rather than one fixed answer.

questions.question: Sort each approach into helpful or unhelpful for solving a complex problem.

items.text: Insisting there is only one possible answer
Testing ideas against the real situation
Refusing to consider any new idea
Copying last year's plan without thought

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Helpful: generate options, test against reality, combine techniques. Unhelpful: assuming one answer, refusing new ideas, copying blindly.

questions.question: What is a sensible first step when facing a complex business problem?
options: Understand and define the problem fully before solving it
Pick the first idea and act immediately
questions.expected: Understand and define the problem fully before solving it
questions.memo: Defining the problem properly first prevents solving the wrong problem and guides the search for good solutions.

questions.question: Thesis: 'Creative thinking is essential in a dynamic, fast-changing business environment.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: Creative thinking is essential in a dynamic, fast-changing business environment.

pool.text: New problems have no ready-made answers, so fresh ideas are needed
It helps a business adapt faster than competitors
It opens up new opportunities as conditions change
Creative thinking guarantees a business never fails
Brainstorming meetings often have nice biscuits
A changing environment never affects a business

questions.memo: The strong reasons are that new problems need fresh ideas, faster adaptation, and new opportunities. The others overclaim, are irrelevant, or are false.

questions.question: _________ thinking generates fresh options that go beyond the obvious answer.
questions.memo: Creative thinking deliberately moves beyond the obvious to produce new, useful options.

questions.question: Why might combining several techniques help solve a complex problem?
options: Different techniques surface different ideas and angles
Using more techniques always wastes time
One technique can never produce ideas
questions.expected: Different techniques surface different ideas and angles
questions.memo: Each technique looks at the problem differently, so combining them produces a richer set of possible solutions.

questions.question: True or false: Even for complex problems, ideas should still be evaluated against the real business situation.
questions.memo: However creative an idea, it must be checked against the business's resources, costs and conditions before being used.

questions.question: Sort each problem into whether routine thinking can solve it or it needs creative thinking.

items.text: Re-ordering stock that has run low
Finding a new market after the main one collapses
Reinventing a product customers no longer want
Responding to a sudden disruptive new technology

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Familiar, repeatable tasks suit routine thinking; new, unfamiliar challenges need creative thinking.

questions.question: What does it mean that a business environment is 'dynamic'?
options: Its conditions change quickly and often
questions.expected: Its conditions change quickly and often
questions.memo: A dynamic environment is one that changes rapidly, so businesses must keep adapting.

questions.question: How does creative thinking help a business cope with rapid change?
options: It finds new ways to adapt, compete and seize opportunities
It freezes the business in place
It removes the need to make decisions
questions.expected: It finds new ways to adapt, compete and seize opportunities
questions.memo: Creative thinking generates the new responses a business needs to adapt and find opportunity when conditions shift.

questions.question: Solving a problem presented in a case _________ tests a learner's ability to apply creative thinking.
questions.memo: A case study gives a realistic situation in which to apply problem-solving and creative thinking.

questions.question: A delivery business is hit at once by fuel hikes, a driver shortage and a new rival. What is the best creative-thinking response?
options: Generate and test several combined options (e.g. route software, training, new services) against the real situation
Pick the first idea that comes to mind and ignore the rest
Copy a competitor's plan without checking if it fits
questions.expected: Generate and test several combined options (e.g. route software, training, new services) against the real situation
questions.memo: A complex, multi-part problem calls for generating several ideas, combining them, and testing them against the business's reality.

questions.question: Why is applying a single fixed answer often wrong for a complex business problem?
options: Complex problems have many factors, so one rigid answer usually misses important parts
Fixed answers are always the most creative
Complex problems never have any solution
questions.expected: Complex problems have many factors, so one rigid answer usually misses important parts
questions.memo: Because complex problems involve many interacting factors, a single rigid answer typically overlooks key aspects.

questions.question: Why are advanced problem-solving skills emphasised at Grade 12 level?
options: Real business challenges are complex and changing, so deeper, combined thinking is needed
Because simple recall is all business ever requires
Because problems disappear on their own
Because creativity is banned in business
questions.expected: Real business challenges are complex and changing, so deeper, combined thinking is needed
questions.memo: Grade 12 builds advanced problem-solving because real business problems are complex and dynamic, needing deeper, combined creative thinking.

questions.question: Which process best reflects creative problem-solving in a complex situation?
options: Define the problem, generate many options, test them against reality, then choose and act
Act first and only think if it fails
Choose the cheapest option without thought
Refuse to consider more than one idea
questions.expected: Define the problem, generate many options, test them against reality, then choose and act
questions.memo: Strong creative problem-solving defines the problem, generates options, evaluates them against the real situation, and then implements the best.
